results.title: Are Perpetual Points Sufficient for Locating Hidden Attractors
results.text:
2017 · Fahimeh Nazarimehr, Batool Saedi, Sajad Jafari · International Journal of Bifurcation and Chaos · 62 citations · Journal Article
TL;DR: This note demonstrates some examples where PPs cannot locate their hidden attractors.
Abstract: Perpetual Points (PPs) have been introduced as an interesting new topic in nonlinear dynamics, and there is a conjecture that these points can be used to find hidden attractors. This note demonstrates some examples where PPs cannot locate their hidden attractors.

results.text:

Abstract: A new class of critical points, termed as perpetual points, where acceleration becomes zero but the velocity remains non-zero, are observed in dynamical systems. The velocity at these points is either maximum or minimum or of inflection behavior.These points also show the bifurcation behavior as parameters of the system vary. These perpetual points are useful for locating the hidden oscillating attractors as well as co-existing attractors. results.title: Describing chaotic attractors: Regular and perpetual points.
results.text:
2018 · Dawid Dudkowski, Awadhesh Prasad, Tomasz Kapitaniak · Chaos · 21 citations · Journal Article
TL;DR: The correlation between regular and perpetual points, as well as their relation with phase space, is analyzed, showing the potential usefulness of both types of points in the qualitative description of co-existing states.
Abstract: We study the concepts of regular and perpetual points for describing the behavior of chaotic attractors in dynamical systems. The idea of these points, which have been recently introduced to theoretical investigations, is thoroughly discussed and extended into new types of models. We analyze the correlation between regular and perpetual points, as well as their relation with phase space, showing the potential usefulness of both types of points in the qualitative description of co-existing states. TL;DR: In this paper, the Conley index is used to construct a simplicial model and a surjective semi-conjugacy for a large class of attractors, and the essential features of this construction are that the modelM can be explicitly described and that the finite amount of information needed to construct it is computable.

2026 · Sajad Jafari, Aboozar Soheylifar, Atiyeh Bayani · International Journal of Bifurcation and Chaos · Journal Article
TL;DR: Chaotic dynamics in 3D quadratic systems without fixed points and perpetual points are extremely rare and structurally fragile, emerging only under highly restricted transitional conditions, despite the absence of fixed points already being uncommon.
Abstract: This study examines the emergence of chaotic dynamics in Three-Dimensional (3D) quadratic systems that lack both fixed points and perpetual points.
